where: crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/job.rs (Jobs::started_unit, Jobs::compiled, Jobs::worked), crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/job/said.rs, crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/unit.rs (Writer::read_outside, Writer::env_named)
what: Making a certificate's `said` from a build that compiled met three facts: (1) what a build says is in its scheduler's order (a package's line at its first unit's begin, a unit's diagnostics at its end) and its `Work` counts that build's own effort, so two builds of the same reads say different bytes and the second is refused as two answers under one key; (2) `Writer::read_outside` names only the paths under the build's directories of outputs (the kept answer left the rest to the watches as a whole, which a certificate does not have), so a build script's read of a file elsewhere outside the views is in no read-list; (3) `Writer::env_named` and `read_outside` are `Err` for a build in which a build script ran, so a first build with build scripts still writes no certificate.
cost: `said` had to be given an order of its own (the plan's) and a `Work` of no work, which is not byte for byte what a walk says (a walk's order is its scheduler's); (2) is a wrong hit waiting to happen and (3) keeps reth's first build from writing; both are open
cause: a build's words are a stream in the order things happened, with one build's counters in it, and were the only form of its answer; the steps' reads were collected for the watches' lane, which needed only those under the outputs
whys: why two answers: the answer is filed under its reads' digests and `said` held the scheduler's order and the build's counts
why was the order the scheduler's: units say their words as they begin and end, for a live client
why is there no plan-ordered form: nothing but the live client read a build's words before the certificate
why are reads elsewhere unnamed: the kept answer asked the watches whether anything at all changed outside, and named only what it had to set aside
class: a value filed under a content key that holds something of the run that made it (its order, its counts, its clock)
prevention: what is filed is made by one pure function of the request and the reads (`said::Saying`), with an oracle that two runs leave the same bytes and a planted bug for each thing of the run that could leak in
